name: SPHEREx
fullName: Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer
challengeTitle: Planet X and SPHEREx Sky Change Explorer
challengeDescription: SPHEREx surveys the entire sky every six months in 102 near-infrared bands. Comparing observations taken months apart reveals the dynamic universe: moving asteroids and comets, variable stars, brown dwarfs, transients, and planetary candidates.

scientificPrinciples.title: Detector Bands vs 102 Spectral Channels
scientificPrinciples.body: SPHEREx uses 6 detector arrays equipped with Linear Variable Filters (LVFs). Wavelength varies continuously across the detector field of view rather than being 102 distinct physical filters. Each Level-2 image records a slice of this spectral variation.

scientificPrinciples.title: Strict Temporal Comparability
scientificPrinciples.body: Valid change detection requires reprojecting onto a common celestial WCS and verifying wavelength compatibility (within 2%) before subtracting flux. CSS opacity blending is not scientific difference imaging.

scientificPrinciples.title: Candidate vs Discovery
scientificPrinciples.body: Automated difference and significance algorithms detect statistical outliers (DAOStarFinder). Resampling noise, bad pixels, and PSF variations produce artifacts. A candidate is never a confirmed discovery without human verification.
